title: An etale ring map is quasi-finite at every prime (Stacks 00U5)
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then $S$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra and $R\to S$ is quasi-finite [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] at every prime ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $S$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00U5 (lemma-etale-quasi-finite, line 39456) and its proof (fibre rings are etale over the residue fields, hence finite products of finite separable extensions by Lemma 00U3, so quasi-finite by Lemma 00PM lemma-quasi-finite)

proof.text: Apply AlgebraicGeometry.HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/RingHomProperties.lean:360-364) to the etale Spec morphism, then RingHom.etale_algebraMap (Mathlib/RingTheory/RingHom/Etale.lean:37-38). This gives Algebra.Etale R S. Its finitePresentation instance gives FiniteType and EssFiniteType; its formallyEtale instance gives FormallyUnramified.

The Mathlib instance in RingTheory/Unramified/LocalStructure.lean:330-333 gives Algebra.QuasiFinite R S from EssFiniteType and FormallyUnramified. For every prime p, Algebra.QuasiFinite.finite_fiber makes p.Fiber S finite over p.ResidueField; the instance in RingTheory/QuasiFinite/Basic.lean:77-78 makes that ring Artinian. Its prime spectrum therefore has the discrete topology. These are already proved Mathlib instances, so no product-of-fields theorem is needed.

Choose the inferred FiniteType witness. For arbitrary q, unfold Algebra.IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime. The definition already uses PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber to construct the corresponding fibre prime. The whole fibre spectrum is discrete by the preceding step, so isOpen_discrete proves its singleton open. This proves the unchanged conclusion, including empty spectra and the zero ring.

split_report.summary: Split following Stacks Algebra 00U5 (algebra.tex line 39456; tags 00U5, 00U2, 00U3, 00PM, 00PK verified in tags/tags) in four steps: (1) S finitely presented, hence of finite type, by the ring-level characterization lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine; (2) the fibre kappa(p) (x)_R S is etale over kappa(p) by lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change (00U2 (2)); (3) it is a finite product of finite separable extensions by lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product (00U3), transported to S (x)_R kappa(p) by the swap isomorphism, so Spec F is discrete by lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-product-fields (2); (4) the prime of F over q (lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection) is isolated, which is the definition def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime (isolated point, condition (1) of 00PK); Stacks' final appeal to 00PM (finite fibre => quasi-finite) is replaced by reading the isolated-point condition off directly, as already done in lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points. Statement and stmt_deps kept (correct against 00U5, which states 'an etale ring map is quasi-finite'; the node's 'finitely generated' clause is the 'by definition finite type' sentence of the proof). No new nodes: all cited nodes exist in unit sk-thm-p1. The citer lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-equivalence (step 7) uses only 'R -> B quasi-finite at every prime of B' for an etale B, which the statement gives.
